title: Inter-variant translation and tooling compatibility orchestration
creator: Ari Cohen
description: Maintain a machine-readable compatibility layer that ensures fallback model variants used by smart routing do not introduce silent failure modes. This ticket covers the orchestration around the compatibility matrix: automated checks for tokenizer/vocab mismatches, context-window harmonization, tooling integration (tracing, EV/metrics hooks), and publishing a signed compatibility adjudication we call the 'handshake registry'. The goal is to reduce live fallbacks that cause tokenization drift or tooling breakage when routing across region/tier fallbacks.
background: Smart routing will route requests by region and tier and may fall back to variant models (quantized/trimmed/region-specific). Historically we've had incidents where a fallback variant had a different tokenizer behavior (e.g., different pad/unk token assignments or byte-level segmentation), causing generation regressions and tooling (tracing, evals) misalignment. This task builds the end-to-end orchestration to keep the compatibility matrix current and enforceable in the routing plane.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility registry stores per-variant attributes: tokenizer-vocab-hash, context-window, eos/pad/token mappings, supported tooling hooks
Automated CI job ('compat-sanity') runs on model onboarding and produces a pass/fail + diff artifact stored in S3 and linked to registry
Routing plane rejects or flags fallback candidates with incompatible tokenizer mismatch severity >= medium unless a signed mitigation (normalizer or remap) is present
Golden prompt suite (100 representative prompts across languages and tokenization edge cases) runs in the canary pipeline with <1% semantic regression vs baseline for approved fallbacks
Runbook documented and linked from Console: how to remediate mismatch (remap tables, lightweight tokenizer shim, or model pinning)
tech_decisions: Represent tokenizer parity as a small deterministic fingerprint (vocab hash + edge-case sample tokenization map) stored in registry
Use a preprocessor-based canonicalizer rather than on-the-fly tokenizer replacement in the runtime to avoid performance regression for hot paths
Integrate the compat-sanity job into model onboarding pipeline (GitHub Actions) and emit artifacts to artifact-store with signed metadata
Severity levels for mismatches: info (cosmetic), low (minor detokenization diffs), medium (different pad/unk/eos semantics), high (broken byte-level segmentation)
implementation_plan: Spike (2 days): implement tokenizer fingerprint generator and run across current variant catalog to get baseline
Compat-sanity CI (3 days): build job that executes tokenizer round-trip, golden-prompt runs, and produces JSON artifact
Registry API (3 days): POST/GET compatibility entries, provide signed metadata and verification endpoint
Routing integration (4 days): routing plane consults registry at decision time; implement soft-fail flagging and metrics emission
Remediation helpers (3 days): lightweight normalizer library (python/ts) and PR template for model teams to submit remap tables
rollout_plan: Week 1: Run spinner-mode: generate registry and run compat-sanity across 25% of variants, surface dashboard metrics to Console (no enforcement)
Week 2: Canary enforcement in staging region: block fallbacks with 'high' severity mismatches, notify owning teams
Week 3: Expand enforcement to production tier-routing (non-critical tenants); collect false-positive telemetry and iterate
Week 4: Full enforcement across all routing modes and publish runbook + training session for Solutions/Platform teams
risks: False positives from heuristic fingerprinting could over-block viable fallbacks — mitigate by keeping an 'info/low' bucket and human review workflow
Performance impact if registry lookups are not cached — mitigate via local LRU cache in routing plane and signed TTL on entries
Onboarding burden for model owners — provide templates, automation, and a 2-week open remediation window before hard blocks
testing_notes: Golden prompt suite includes language edge cases, long-prefix scenarios, and byte-level inputs to detect segmentation differences
Add unit tests for fingerprint generator, CI job mocks, and routing-plane cache eviction behavior
Create a synthetic regression harness that simulates tier-routing fallbacks at scale and measures token-level deltas and downstream SDK errors
